---
title: Get started
---

`dazapiz` carries your `az login` into Spark, DuckDB and any Azure REST API,
on top of `azure-identity` and `msal`. This page takes one login all the way
to a Spark session that reads Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2.

None of the code on these pages runs when the site is built: it needs an
Azure account.

## Install

```sh
pip install dazapiz            # Spark configuration, credentials, REST client, az helpers
pip install "dazapiz[duckdb]"  # also the DuckDB secrets in dazapiz.duckdb
```

PySpark is never a dependency: `dazapiz` builds a plain `dict` of Spark
settings, for whichever Spark you already have.

## Log in once

`az_login()` runs `az login --use-device-code` and prints the code to enter
at <https://microsoft.com/devicelogin>. It does nothing when the Azure CLI is
already logged in, so it is safe at the top of a notebook.

```python
from dazapiz import az_login

az_login()
```

```
To sign in, open https://microsoft.com/devicelogin and enter the code ABCD1234.
Logged in to the Azure CLI as you@example.com.
```

`az_is_login()`, `az_account_show()` and `az_logout()` do the rest of what
you would type at a terminal. They need the Azure CLI (`az`) on `PATH`.

## Find the refresh token

`refresh_token_from_az_cli()` reads the refresh token the Azure CLI keeps in
`~/.azure/msal_token_cache.json`, for the account and tenant of its default
subscription, without running `az`:

```python
from dazapiz import refresh_token_from_az_cli

info = refresh_token_from_az_cli()
info
```

```
RefreshTokenInfo(token='<redacted>', client_id='04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46', tenant_id='...', username='you@example.com')
```

The token never prints. It belongs to the Azure CLI's own client ID, which
`info` carries along, so whatever redeems it uses the right one. On Windows,
where the Azure CLI keeps its tokens in the Windows broker, it raises
`UnsupportedPlatformError`; sign in with `DeviceCodeCredential` instead (see
[Browser-hosted sign-in](browser-sign-in.qmd)).

## Spark

`spark_storage_conf()` turns the token into the Hadoop ABFS settings that let
Spark read and write ADLS Gen2 as you:

```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from dazapiz import refresh_token_from_az_cli, spark_storage_conf

conf = spark_storage_conf(refresh_token=refresh_token_from_az_cli())
spark = SparkSession.builder.config(map=conf).getOrCreate()

df = spark.read.parquet("abfss://data@myaccount.dfs.core.windows.net/sales/")
```

The keys start with `spark.hadoop.` so that `SparkSession.builder` passes
them to Hadoop; `prefix=None` gives the bare `fs.azure.*` keys for
`core-site.xml` or `spark.sparkContext._jsc.hadoopConfiguration().set()`.
`storage_account="myaccount"` scopes every key to one account. Printing the
result shows `<redacted>` in place of the token.

## Other ways to authenticate

`auth_type` picks the Hadoop token provider; values not passed come from the
standard `AZURE_*` variables:

| `auth_type` | Who | Reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"refresh_token"` (default) | you, from a sign-in | `refresh_token`, else `$AZURE_REFRESH_TOKEN` |
| `"client_secret"` | a service principal | `$AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `$AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `$AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` |
| `"workload_identity"` | an AKS workload | `$AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `$AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `$AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE` |
| `"managed_identity"` | the VM or cluster's identity | `$AZURE_CLIENT_ID` for a user-assigned one |
| `"shared_key"` | the storage account key | `storage_account`, `account_key` |

```python
conf = spark_storage_conf("client_secret", storage_account="myaccount")
```

The refresh token can also come from somewhere else:
`spark_storage_conf(refresh_token=...)` takes a string, or anything with a
`get_refresh_token()` method, such as `DeviceCodeCredential()` or
`InteractiveBrowserCredential()`.

## The same login elsewhere

- `RefreshTokenCredential(refresh_token_from_az_cli())` is a
  `TokenCredential`: pass it to any Azure SDK client.
- [DuckDB](duckdb.qmd) registers it as an Azure secret.
- [REST client](rest-client.qmd) builds a typed client for one API.
